# Krystian Safjan's Blog

> Practitioner notes by Krystian Safjan, AI/ML technical leader at EY, on building and operating LLM, RAG and ML systems in enterprise environments: evaluation, MLOps, model migration, agentic workflows and engineering leadership.

- [About the author](https://safjan.com/about/)

- [LinkedIn](https://pl.linkedin.com/in/krystiansafjan)
- [GitHub](https://github.com/izikeros)

## LLM Engineering

- [The Real Cost of Model Migration - What Swapping LLMs Actually Requires](https://safjan.com/the-real-cost-of-model-migration-what-swapping-llms-actually-requires/): Model deprecations are routine. What they expose underneath - unmeasured quality, model-coupled prompts, unversioned behavior - rarely is. This post walks through what a migration actually requires -…
- [Prompt Discovery](https://safjan.com/prompt-discovery/): What prompt discovery is: a systematic process for finding and refining prompts that get the desired output from a language model, weighing response quality, model performance and compute cost.
- [Understanding the Differences in Language Models - Transformers vs. Markov Models](https://safjan.com/understanding-differences-gpt-transformers-markov-models/): How Markov models and Transformer models like GPT predict the next character, and why self-attention with variable context beats the fixed context length of Markov models.
- [Problems with Langchain and how to minimize their impact](https://safjan.com/problems-with-Langchain-and-how-to-minimize-their-impact/): Ten common problems with LangChain, such as unnecessary abstractions, poor documentation, inefficient token usage and a focus on demos, and how to use it so these problems have less impact.
- [Leveraging Language Models in Corporate Environments - The Future of Knowledge Management](https://safjan.com/language-models-for-knowledge-management-in-corporate/): Benefits and challenges of using large language models for knowledge management in companies, how to introduce them, and what can slow down their adoption.
- [How to Detect ChatGPT-Generated Text?](https://safjan.com/detection-of-texts-generated-by-large-language-models-like-chatgpt/): Survey of methods for detecting text generated by LLMs like ChatGPT: statistical, syntactic, semantic and hybrid approaches, plus neural, adversarial, attention-based and pre-trained detectors.

Retrieval drift is silent, cumulative and rarely audited. This post…

- [Techniques to Boost RAG Performance in Production](https://safjan.com/techniques-to-boost-rag-performance-in-production/): Techniques to improve RAG performance in production, including hybrid search, chunk summaries, query transformations, embedding fine-tuning, re-ranking, metadata filtering, query routing and handling…
- [From Fixed-Size to NLP Chunking - A Deep Dive into Text Chunking Techniques](https://safjan.com/from-fixed-size-to-nlp-chunking-a-deep-dive-into-text-chunking-techniques/): Text chunking methods for semantic search and RAG: fixed-size windows in characters or tokens, recursive and structure-aware splitting, NLP topic-based chunking, content-aware splitting, and adding…
- [Understanding Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) empowering LLMs](https://safjan.com/understanding-retrieval-augmented-generation-rag-empowering-llms/): An introduction to retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): how adding information from external sources to the prompt helps large language models give accurate and current answers.
- [Easy Text Vectorization With VectorHub and Sentence Transformers](https://safjan.com/text-vectorization-with-vectorhub-and-sentence-transformers/): How to vectorize text with Sentence Transformers, using different embedding models through one consistent API, based on an example that originally used VectorHub.
- [The Best Vector Databases for Storing Embeddings](https://safjan.com/the-best-vector-databases-for-storing-embeddings/): Compares vector databases for storing embeddings, including Chroma, Faiss, Milvus, pgvector, Pinecone, Qdrant, Vespa, Weaviate and DeepLake, with a feature table and recommendations for PoCs and…

## Evaluation & Observability

- [RAG Evaluation with RAGAS and MLflow - A Practical Guide](https://safjan.com/ragas-mlflow-rag-evaluation-tutorial/): "A tutorial on evaluating a minimal LangChain RAG pipeline with RAGAS metrics in MLflow: golden dataset, Faithfulness, Context Precision, Context Recall and Factual Correctness, with OpenAI, Azure…
- [RankFlow plot for retriever visual evaluation](https://safjan.com/rankflow-plot-for-retriever-visual-evaluation/): How to collect document rankings from each re-ranking step of a RAG retriever, using structured logs or callbacks, and visualize rank changes with a rank flow (bump) chart.
- [Open Source LLM Observability Tools and Platforms](https://safjan.com/open-source-llm-observability-tools-and-platforms/): What LLM observability is, which functions an observability solution should provide, and a list of open source tools such as Langfuse, Phoenix, OpenLLMetry, Evidently, Giskard and LangKit.
- [Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic Evaluation - What's the Best Way to Measure Embedding Quality?](https://safjan.com/measure-quality-of-embeddings-intrinsic-vs-extrinsic/): How to measure the quality of word and sentence embeddings with intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation, and the strengths and limitations of each approach.
- [Comprehensive Guide to Interpreting R², MSE, and RMSE for Regression Models.](https://safjan.com/interpreting-r2-mse-rmse-for-regression-models/): How to interpret R², MSE and RMSE together when evaluating regression models, and what different combinations of their values tell you about the model.
- [Pro Tips for Diagnosing Regression Model Errors](https://safjan.com/regression-model-errors-plot/): Plots for diagnosing regression model errors: residual plot, histogram of residuals, scale-location, Q-Q, leverage, Cook's distance, actual vs. predicted, and MAE vs. parameter.
- [Understanding Micro and Macro Averages in Multiclass Multilabel Problems](https://safjan.com/micro-and-macro-averages-in-multiclass-multilabel-problems/): The difference between multiclass and multilabel problems, how micro and macro averages of metrics are calculated, and when to use each.
- [Metrics Used to Compare Histograms](https://safjan.com/metrics-to-compare-histograms/): Metrics for comparing histograms, including Chi-squared distance, Earth Mover's distance and Kullback-Leibler divergence, with Python examples of how to calculate them.
- [Kaggle Evaluation Metrics Used for Regression Problems](https://safjan.com/kaggle-evaluation-metrics-used-for-regression-problems/): Eight evaluation metrics used in Kaggle regression competitions: AE, MAE, weighted MAE, Pearson and Spearman correlation, RMSE, RMSLE and MCRMSE, with their definitions.

Here is when it works, when it doesn't, and what I think about it after…
- [How Agile Can Kill Creativity in Data Science team?](https://safjan.com/how-agile-can-kill-creativity-in-data-science-team/): Ways Agile can hinder creativity in data science teams, such as tight sprint deadlines, focus on deliverables, lack of autonomy and rigid processes, and practices that help reduce these effects.
- [The Role and Responsibilities of a Forward Deployed Engineer - Bridging the Gap Between Software Products and Customer Needs](https://safjan.com/the-role-and-responsibilities-of-a-forward-deployed-engineer/): What a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) does: working directly with customers to adapt enterprise software to their needs, and collaborating with engineering, product and sales teams.
- [Mastering the Kanban Method - Unveiling the Hidden Gems of Effective Kanban Board Usage](https://safjan.com/mastering-kanban-method/): The core Kanban principles, common mistakes like ignoring WIP limits, and lesser-known tips for Kanban boards such as classes of service, marking blocked tasks and swimlanes.
- [Rethinking the Link Between Speech and Expertise](https://safjan.com/illusion-of-expertise/): Why eloquent speech is often taken as a sign of knowledge and expertise, and why this assumption can be wrong.
- [New Cognitive Skills in the Age of AI Tailored Information Presentation](https://safjan.com/pros-and-cons-of-reliance-on-ai-generating-models/): A speculative essay on new cognitive skills people may develop when large language models present information tailored to them, such as processing complex information faster.
- [The Impact of Search Engines and AI Generative Models on Mental and Cognitive Capabilities](https://safjan.com/impact_of_google_search_and_llms_on_methal_capabilities/): Positive and negative effects of search engines and generative AI models on memory, problem solving and other cognitive capabilities, and what this means for how we use them.
- [Common Types of Data Science Projects](https://safjan.com/common-types-of-data-science-projects/): Five common types of data science projects (individual, collaborative, shared notebook, production-ready and research) and good practices for each.
- [MLOps Certifications - A Comprehensive Guide](https://safjan.com/mlops-certifications-a-comprehensive-guide/): MLOps-related certifications from AWS and Google Cloud, whether they are worth the effort and money, and free MLOps courses and certificates.
- [Roles in MLOps](https://safjan.com/roles-in-mlops/): Specialized roles in MLOps and their responsibilities: model deployment, data pipeline, model monitoring, model governance, ML infrastructure and ML platform engineers.
- [50 Questions for MLOps Engineer Job Interview](https://safjan.com/50-questions-for-MLOps-engineer-job-interview/): 50 questions for an MLOps engineer job interview, covering model deployment and management, data pipelines, monitoring and related topics.
- [MLOps Roles of the Future](https://safjan.com/mlops_roles_of_the_future/): Possible future MLOps specializations: explainable AI, federated and edge learning, reinforcement learning, ML in IoT and IIoT, and model explainability and fairness.
- [Is MLOps a Good Career?](https://safjan.com/is-mlops-good-career/): Pros and cons of a career in MLOps, including demand for skilled people, earning potential, type of work and growth opportunities.

## Responsible AI

- [Attacking Differential Privacy Using the Correlation Between the Features](https://safjan.com/attacking-differential-privacy-using-the-correlation-between-the-features/): How an attacker can use correlation between features to reconstruct data protected with differential privacy, with a Python demo on the age and education-num features and ways to mitigate the attack.
- [Are LIME Explanations Any Useful?](https://safjan.com/are-lime-explanations-any-useful/): What LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations) is, where it is used in practice to explain black-box models, and its benefits and limitations.
- [Explaining AI - The Key Differences Between LIME and SHAP Methods](https://safjan.com/explaining-ai-the-key-differences-between-lime-and-shap-methods/): Key differences between LIME and SHAP for explainable AI: model-agnostic vs. model-specific use, local vs. global explanations, kernel-based vs. game-theoretic approach, and the…
- [LIME - Understanding How This Method for Explainable AI Works](https://safjan.com/how-the-lime-method-for-explainable-ai-works/): How LIME explains individual model predictions step by step: selecting an instance, perturbing it to create similar samples, and fitting a simple local model to find the important features.
- [SHAP - Understanding How This Method for Explainable AI Works](https://safjan.com/how-the-shap-method-for-explainable-ai-works/): What SHAP is, how it uses Shapley values to attribute a model's prediction to individual features, and how to apply it in practice.
- [KernelShap and TreeShap - Two Most Popular Variations of the SHAP Method](https://safjan.com/kernelshap-treeshap-two-most-popular-variations-of-the-shap-method/): How KernelSHAP and TreeSHAP work around the exponential cost of exact Shapley values in the original SHAP method, and how the two differ in approach and supported models.
- [LIME Tutorial](https://safjan.com/lime-tutorial/): A tutorial on using LIME to explain predictions of a random forest classifier trained on the Iris dataset, including visualizing which features drive each decision.
- [Understanding AI with ELI5 - Demystifying Decisions (tutorial)](https://safjan.com/eli5-tutorial/): A tutorial on explaining models with the ELI5 library on the Titanic dataset, using permutation importance for a random forest and feature weights for logistic regression.
- [Evaluation of Interpretability for Explainable AI](https://safjan.com/evaluation-of-interpretability-for-explainable-ai/): Three levels of evaluating interpretability in machine learning (application, human and function level), with tools and methods for assessing model explanations.

- [Git Hooks](https://safjan.com/git-hooks/): An example of setting up a Git pre-commit hook manually, with a Python script that runs isort, and the same setup done with the pre-commit tool.
- [Time Tracking Apps](https://safjan.com/time-tracking-apps/): The time tracking setup that works for me: GTime for logging activities manually, with the open source ActivityWatch to fill in entries I forgot to log.
- [Add Logo to Notebook Header Cell](https://safjan.com/add-logo-to-notebook-header/): A short HTML snippet that places a project logo next to the title in the first markdown cell of a Jupyter notebook.
- [Git Add - Stage Changes in Various Ways](https://safjan.com/git-add/): A short note on the differences between git add -A, git add . and git add -u, and how git add behaves since Git 2.0.
- [Pre-Commit Hooks](https://safjan.com/git-pre-commit-hooks/): How to install pre-commit and configure Git hooks in a .pre-commit-config.yaml file, using hooks from the pre-commit-hooks repository.
- [Python - Convert Docstring Styles](https://safjan.com/python-convert-docstring-styles/): How to convert docstrings between styles, for example from numpy-style to google-style, with Pyment, which supports javadoc, reST, numpydoc and google formats.
- [Python - Docstrings Styles](https://safjan.com/python-docstrings-styles/): Examples of the most popular Python docstring styles (Google, NumPy, reST) and which formats are supported by Pyment, pdoc3 and PyCharm.
- [Python - Project Documentation From the Code With Pdoc3](https://safjan.com/python-documentation-with-pdoc3/): Commands for generating HTML documentation from Python code with pdoc3 and opening it in the browser, with links to alternatives such as MkDocs Material, Docusaurus and VitePress.
- [Git - Autocommit on File Changes](https://safjan.com/git-autocommit-on-file-changes/): Tools that commit changes automatically when files in a watched folder change, such as gitwatch, gwatch, etckeeper and git-wip, which I looked at to keep a history of my notes.
- [Box-Cox Transform - Normalizing Non-Normal Data](https://safjan.com/box-cox-transformation/): How the Box-Cox transformation makes non-normal data closer to normal with a power function, with Python examples on synthetic data and use cases in customer, financial and medical data.
